feedback:
Approving this candidate. It is a clean single-variable test of speed: the wide sensor span is kept, and base_speed drops from 1.4 to 1.1 with kp 2.0, ki 0.4 and kd 0.15 unchanged. Evidence: iteration 3 (wide span, x = ±0.07 m) cut line_loss_events from 1 to 0 on every track, which supports the narrow-span hypothesis. But all 60 trials still went off_track with 0 finishes, and max_error sat at 0.0625 to 0.0629 on oval and s-bend and 0.061 on slalom, just past the 0.06 m limit. Progress is very low: s-bend 0.042 and slalom 0.035, which is roughly the first 0.2 m of the course. Oval reached 0.188. Changing kp, ki and sensor span did not move max_error much, so the remaining cause may be speed-dependent. Iteration 3 scored 37.88, slightly below the best raced score of 38.61 (iteration 1), so it is not yet an improvement. The speed cut will lengthen completion time, which only matters once the robot stays on the line, so the trade is acceptable for this test.

What to change after the race, depending on what it shows:
- If max_error falls below 0.06 on s-bend and slalom and progress rises clearly above 0.14 on at least one track, keep base_speed near 1.1 to 1.2 as the stable point. Then raise it in small steps (for example 1.25, then 1.4) while watching max_error, so the speed recovers without crossing the limit.
- If max_error stays near 0.061 to 0.063 at speed 1.1, speed is not the main cause. Test sensor y placement next by moving the array closer to the axle (y about 0.02 instead of 0.05), keeping the wide span. A kd change (for example 0.3) is the alternative if y placement does not help.
- If line_loss_events returns to 1 or more at speed 1.1, return to the wide span and try line_loss = search_right or search_left, which has still never been tested.
requested_changes: If max_error drops below 0.06 on s-bend and slalom at base_speed 1.1 with progress above 0.14, keep the wide span and step base_speed up gradually (1.25, then 1.4) while checking that max_error stays under 0.06.

If max_error stays near 0.061 to 0.063 at base_speed 1.1, speed is not the main cause (iterations 0 to 3 all showed the same pinned max_error). Move sensor y from 0.05 to about 0.02 m, keeping the x span at ±0.07 m, so the array sits closer to the axle and its lateral reach changes.
If line_loss_events rises again at the lower speed, keep the wide span and set line_loss = search_right or search_left in place of last_direction, which has never been tested.
